poc_test_matrix: Goals: validate throughput guarantees and latency SLOs under production mix. Test types: 1) Steady-state load: 120 concurrent sessions, average 3 turns/session, 600-900 tokens/turn; run 8 hours. 2) Burst load: simulate port-event burst with 400 concurrent sessions for 30 minutes. 3) Soak test: 72-hour steady run at 80% of expected throughput to catch memory leaks and KV-caching regressions. 4) Model-fallback verification: route 15% of requests to cheaper quantized variant and measure quality/regression. Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 latency (token and turn), tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory headroom, error & retry rate. Deliverables: raw traces, per-route dashboards, tail-latency distribution, cost per 1k tokens with config used.
sla_needs: Requested SLOs: p95 < 250ms for short-turn prompts (<256 tokens), p99 < 600ms under steady-state for mixed-turn sizes. Uptime SLA: 99.95% monthly for Dedicated capacity. Required contractual items: credit for missed SLOs, defined fallback behavior (auto-route to alternate capacity tier), compliance addendum for data residency and audit logs.
decision_criteria: 1) Can Redwood demonstrate consistent p99 latency under the 72-hour soak at target concurrency? 2) Is reserved GPU planning cost predictable and does reserved capacity allow 2x headroom + burst scaling? 3) Is vendor contract acceptable for data residency/KMS and subprocessor commitments? 4) Measured output quality when using quantized fallback must be within business threshold (manual eval set). 5) Operational visibility: token-level cost breakdown and per-route tracing are required.
